description: Gives the text of a letter for a tenant to send their landlord, with [bracketed] gaps to fill in: "first-report" to report a repair in writing for the first time, "chaser" when it was reported and nothing has happened, "complaint" to make a formal complaint under the landlord’s complaints procedure (citing section 11 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 in England, or sections 91 and 92 of the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016 in Wales), or "awaabs-law" to ask a council or housing association in England to deal with a hazard under Awaab’s Law. The Awaab’s Law letter is given only to a tenant of a council or housing association in England with a tenancy (not a licence, shared ownership or a long lease). It never takes the tenant’s name, address or details: fill in the gaps with them. The letters state facts and make a request; they promise no outcome.

country.description: Where the home is: "england" (default) or "wales". Wales has its own housing law, and the complaint letter cites a different Act.

landlord.description: "social" for a council or housing association (default), or "private" for a private landlord or letting agent.

tenure.description: How the tenant occupies the home: "tenancy", "licence" (some supported or temporary housing), "shared_or_lease" (shared ownership or a long lease) or "unsure" (default). Only a tenancy gets the Awaab’s Law letter.
